_note: Деталь 3 — Zone 3 cathode flange (01_01 §1 + 02_02 §1.2). Flange Ø25 frozen (HW.8 axial freeze). Shank Ø9 + thickness 3 = PLACEHOLDER (HW.8 bench). Barbs reuse the §4.3 Zone-3 lock with the SAME local ratchet profile as Zone 1 (the ±1 direction knob was removed 2026-09-13, 00_07 HW.26). Bayonet lugs mate the Радом (Деталь 4, фаза 2). Cathode catalytic = side/perimeter (O₂), a strip that stands ABOVE the bark with a non-catalytic buffer below it (01_04 §3.1, ratified 2026-09-18 — the flange is no longer flush with the bark); pogo = top face (Hard Gold coating, not geometry). The top face carries the ONE O-ring groove of the capsule seal (00_07 HW.33 branch (а), applied 2026-09-14): depth, width and radii are DERIVED from the `o_ring` block and the socket fields shared with the radome (CathodeFlange.ORingGroove*) — nothing about the groove is stored here, so nothing about it can go stale.
name: cathode_flange

tolerances.fit: H7/s6 (canon's nominal class only - and the class itself is open: the tree's only band, 5-34 um, is an H7/r6 read, 00_07 HW.3)

notes.material: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) - the standing baseline, not a settled choice: the V-free perimeter rule (ratified 2026-09-17, 01_02 2.5) covers this part, so V-free replaces 4V here if the alloy bake-off winner has an endurance limit at least that of 4V; otherwise this part stays 4V
notes.process: CNC from wrought bar, OR SLM/DMLS followed by a MANDATORY HIP - the same cycle and the same furnace load as the Zone-1 anode, BEFORE the channel and grooves are finish-machined (01_02 1.7, Zone 3 row, ratified 2026-09-18). EBM is not planned: if EBM is what you offer, say so, and only then does HIP become optional (hot build platform). The 'precision less critical' allowance of 01_02 1.7 applies to the FLANGE DISC only (flat O25 face, roughness = ECSA advantage) — it does NOT extend to the bus channel, which is the part's primary datum and is machined after printing (see post-process). Reading it part-wide licenses an as-printed bore and contradicts note 5. Quote the route you would use; if bar, name the wrought standard you machine from (00_07 HW.23).
notes.post_process: CONTACT PLATING: NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM - which spots are plated, by what process and to what thickness is an open decision (02_02 1.3), so do not plate from this sheet. There is NO anode pad on this part: the anode contact is the end face of the bus wire (O1.0) inside the channel, and everything around the bore on this face is cathode metal; build tip-down (01_01 4.3 A: the barbs self-support on this SEPARATE print) - which leaves the O25 disc above the O9 shank as a flat down-facing overhang needing supports; which face they land on, and whether that face is functional, is open (00_07 HW.26) | bus channel O1.35: MACHINE after printing to the tolerance block (primary datum, 0.05 concentricity/runout) - NOT as-printed. The nominal was OPENED 1.30 -> 1.35 by verdict (00_07 HW.34, 2026-09-11) so the rod+liner stack (1.0 + 2x0.15 = 1.30) enters with a real 50 um diametral clearance instead of the zero the arithmetic used to allow; the change rides this EXISTING machining operation, it does not add one. ATTENTION - the DIAMETRAL TOLERANCE BAND on this bore is NOT SPECIFIED anywhere in canon and is not derivable: 50 um may fall inside the tolerance of the extruded PEEK tube itself, whose supplier holds ID/OD and not the wall we froze. It is a question to the vendor (00_07 HW.34), so quote your achievable band rather than reading a default into the blank | bus channel ENTRY EDGE (the shank end face, opposite the flange face, where the liner-covered bus rod enters): a RADIUS, NOT a chamfer. The rod reaches that mouth at a shallow angle, far below a lead-in chamfer's 30-45 deg, so it never lands on a chamfer - it bears on the line where the chamfer meets the bore; a chamfer only moves that edge, a radius removes it. RADIUS VALUE: NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM - choosing one needs a contact model that does not exist yet (00_07 HW.34), so state the edge radius you can produce at the entry of this channel and how you verify it; a sharp or chamfered edge is not a reading of this blank | bus channel EXIT EDGE (the pogo face, where the tube ends flush): the same rule - a RADIUS, NOT a chamfer; RADIUS VALUE: NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM (ratified 2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.34) | O-RING GROOVE on the top (pogo) face - the ONE face seal of the capsule (02_02 3.2 / 3.5, 00_07 HW.33 branch (a), applied 2026-09-14): MACHINE after printing. Depth 1.344 = CS 1.78 x (1 - 0.245 ratified squeeze); width 2.315 = ring section 2.489 mm2 / (0.80 gland fill x depth); cut between r 8.085 and r 10.4, i.e. inside the radome's seal land (r 7.785-10.7) with 0.3 of land on each side. All of these are DERIVED from the o_ring block, none is typed. The radome rim is FLAT and lands on this face as the seal datum, so the squeeze is this depth ALONE. DEPTH TOLERANCE: NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM - the whole O-ring chain (this depth + the flatness of this face + the flatness of the radome rim, RSS) must stay within +/-98 um, so the question to you is 'can you hold +/-0.05 on this depth', never a general-tolerance grade (00_07 HW.33). The gland fill 80 % is RATIFIED (2026-09-17, 00_07 HW.33); its review trigger is a board outline wider than the O15.57 rim cavity (00_07 HW.9) - the WIDTH moves with the fill (85 % -> 2.178, 90 % -> 2.057), the depth does not
notes.surface_finish: PER-SURFACE, not one finish for the whole part (01_02 1.3): catalytic side/perimeter = EAAE dual-scale micro Sa 0.5-5 um + nano Sv 50-500 nm (Step 4, Laccase/ZIF ECSA) - NO PEP and NO H2O2 passivation on that face (Steps 6-7); outer jacket = PEP smoothing to Ra 0.4 um max (Step 7) before ZnO-Ta PEO; pogo top face = MASKED during EAAE; its contact plating is NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM (see post-process), and the PEEK isolation ring 02_02 1.2 requires on this face is NOT in this geometry (solid Ti top face; open, 00_07 HW.34). Sand-blasting is admissible on THIS part (Zone 3, line-of-sight geometry, Step 3), unlike the Zone-1 gyroid.
notes.coating_restriction: Catalytic face (Laccase + ZIF-nanozyme + PTFE-GDL): ZnO-Ta, self-healing 8-HQ and biomimetic (Zn-HAp/chitosan) ALL FORBIDDEN - bare Ti only, any dielectric blocks DET. Outer jacket: ZnO-Ta + 8-HQ allowed. NOT on PEEK. (01_02 3.6)
notes.lattice_spec: Not applicable - solid flange disc with a central bus channel, no lattice. (The lattice lives in the Zone-1 anode this part mates to, cem/anchor_zone1.*.json)
notes.inspection: SEM of the catalytic face BEFORE shipment (01_02 1.5, factory obligation): x5,000 for micro-roughness (report the AREAL Sa of the 01_02 1.2 acceptance row, not a profile Ra) and x50,000 for nano-pores Sv - if nano-pores are not visible at x50,000 the etch is insufficient and EAAE (01_02 1.3 Step 4) is repeated; the x500 frame of 01_02 1.5 is for gyroid macro-pores and has no subject on this part. Bus channel: MACHINED after printing to the tolerance block (primary datum, 0.05 concentricity/runout) and it must accept the 0.15 mm structural liner (01_01 1.4) - an as-printed bore fails this part. Its own diametral band is listed as bore_dia with BOTH limits NOT SPECIFIED: that blank is the open vendor question of 00_07 HW.34, not a licence to accept any bore that passes concentricity. PEP is confined to the outer jacket: measure Ra <= 0.4 um THERE and nowhere else, because PEP on the catalytic face would cut away exactly the ECSA Step 4 just created (01_02 1.3 Step 7). Contact plating is NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM (see post-process), so there is no plated spot to inspect on this sheet; the PEEK isolation ring 02_02 1.2 requires on this face is NOT in this geometry (solid Ti top face; open, 00_07 HW.34), so there is no bare ring to inspect until it is. ATTENTION: the batch-level SEM ACCEPTANCE CRITERION - what morphology passes, as opposed to which frames to shoot - does not exist in canon yet and is an open leg (00_07 HW.1); do not read its absence as a pass. ANODE-TO-CATHODE RESISTANCE, added 2026-09-12: measure it on the ASSEMBLED anchor before shipment. The bus rod runs up this channel isolated by a 0.15 mm PEEK liner, and a missing or wear-through liner shorts anode to cathode (~0.5 V) - that is a NODE failure, not a degradation, and no direct control on a missing tube exists otherwise (00_07 HW.34, FMEA row #22 carries D=8 for exactly this reason). Cheapest mitigation in the whole register and it belongs on THIS part's acceptance sheet, because the channel is here. SEAM CONTINUITY, same fixture and the same probe on the pad (ratified 2026-09-18, 00_07 HW.34): 4-wire DC resistance from the wire end face to the anode lattice, after this flange is pressed on and BEFORE enzyme functionalisation - no other path joins pad and anode then, so an open reads unambiguously. Pass = continuity, open = fail; numeric threshold NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM until the alloy is chosen. It screens an OPEN seam only, never a fatigue crack. O-RING GROOVE (top face): measure the depth 1.344 against the tolerance you quoted (post-process) and the FLATNESS of the top face across the seal land r 7.785-10.7 - the radome rim lands there as the seal datum and both faces share one +/-98 um chain (00_07 HW.33); o_ring_groove_depth is listed with BOTH limits NOT SPECIFIED on purpose, that blank is the open shop question, not a licence
extra: Anode contact = the end face of the bus wire (O1.0) inside the channel - NOT a pad on this part. The concept pad O4-5 (02_02 1.3) is not in this geometry, and its plating waits on an open decision (02_02 1.3, 00_07 HW.8), so nothing on this face is plated from this sheet
02_02 1.2 requires a PEEK isolation ring >=1.5 mm centre<->outer (short-circuit guard); this geometry does NOT provide it - the top face is solid Ti to the bore edge (open, 00_07 HW.34)
